Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:10:1.english: They taught [this] only - [Concerning the limit of] within [the time] that he can show [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:10:2.hebrew: אלא לוקח - שמקחו בידו ויכול להראות':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:10:2.english: Only a buyer - For his purchase is in his hand, and he is able to show it [to a merchant or to his relative].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:10:3.hebrew: מוכר - שאין בידו מה להראות ולימלך, אינו מכיר באונאתו עד שיראה טלית אחרת כדמותה נמכרת בדמים יקרים. הלכך, לעולם חוזר, אם לא נתייקרו טליתות בינתים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:10:3.english: A seller - Since he has nothing in his possession to show and to consult [about], he does not recognize the overreaching [against him] until he sees another cloak like it being sold for a high price. Therefore, he may always renege, provided that cloaks have not risen in price in the meantime.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:1:1.english: And according to Rabbi Tarfon too, there is an immediate waiver - [Of] less than a third.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:1:2.hebrew: אמאי חזרו - הא כל היום דר' טרפון בשליש הוא דקאמר להו, ויזהרו מאונאת שליש ויהא הכל מחילה לאלתר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:1:2.english: Why did they revert - Surely, [the rule of] "all day" of Rabbi Tarfon was stated by him regarding [an overcharge of] a third; so let them be careful [to avoid] an overcharge of a third, and everything [less than a third] will be a waiver immediately.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:2:1.hebrew: משתות ועד שליש לרבי טרפון - הויא אונאה כשתות עצמה לרבנן. ואינו חולק על חכמים, אלא דבטול מקח דידהו משוי להו אונאה וידו על העליונה, ואליבא דרבנן שניהם חוזרין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:2:1.english: From one-sixth until one-third according to Rabbi Tarfon - [It] is [a case of] overcharging, like one-sixth itself according to the Rabbis. And he does not disagree with the Sages, except that their [case of] voiding the sale he treats as overcharging, and [the defrauded party] has the upper hand, whereas according to the Rabbis, both [parties] may retract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:2:2.hebrew: אי הכי - דר' טרפון אבטול מקח לחודיה פליג:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:2:2.english: If so - That Rabbi Tarfon disagrees only regarding voiding the sale.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:2:3.english: For what did they rejoice - [Meaning,] initially.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:3:1.english: Resolve - For [this can be resolved] from the fact that they rejoiced.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:3:2.hebrew: ביטול מקח לרבנן - דמיבעיא לן לקמן אי לעולם חוזר או בכדי שיראה. תפשוט דמדשמחו, דלרבנן לעולם חוזר; וכי אמר להו ר' טרפון אונאה — והם היו סבורין דבכדי שיראה ס"ל באונאה — שמחו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:3:2.english: Nullification of the transaction according to the Rabbis - Regarding which we have a dilemma later [in the Gemara], whether one may always renege or [only] within the time it takes to show [the item to a merchant or relative]. Resolve [it], for from the fact that they rejoiced, [it follows] that according to the Rabbis one may always renege; and when Rabbi Tarfon said to them [that it is] exploitation — and they thought that he holds [that one may renege only] within the time it takes to show [it] in [a case of] exploitation — they rejoiced.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:3:3.hebrew: כי אמר להו כל היום חזרו - חדא, דבין לעולם חוזר ובין שהות כל היום הנאה פורתא היא לדידהו, דשהות הרבה יש לימלך כל היום. ועוד, אונאה יתר על שתות לא שכיחא, וקמפסיד להו בשתות עצמה — לרבנן בכדי שיראה, ולדידיה כל היום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:3:3.english: When he said to them "the entire day," they reverted - Firstly, [the difference] between "he may always renege" and a timeframe of the entire day is [only] a minor benefit to them, because the entire day is a long timeframe to consult [with others]. And furthermore, exploitation of more than one-sixth is uncommon, and he causes them a loss regarding [exploitation of] one-sixth itself — [for] according to the Rabbis [the timeframe is only] enough time for him to show [the item], whereas according to him [it is] the entire day.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:4:1.hebrew: דאי ס"ד בטול מקח לרבנן - כאונאה בכדי שיראה, ואין בין אונאה לבטול מקח אלא דבאונאה ידו על העליונה, ובבטול מקח שניהם חוזרין. כי משוי רבי טרפון לבטול מקח אונאה, אין זו טובה להם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:4:1.english: For if it enters your mind [that] nullification of the transaction according to the Rabbis - [is] like exploitation, within the time that he can show [it to a merchant or relative], and there is no [difference] between exploitation and nullification of the transaction except that in exploitation [the defrauded party] has the upper hand, whereas in nullification of the transaction both of them can retract. When Rabbi Tarfon makes nullification of the transaction [into] exploitation, this is not a benefit to them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:4:2.hebrew: שמחו בשתות עצמה כו' - דהא דאמרן משתות ועד שליש לר"ט כשתות לרבנן, משתות ומעלה אמרו, ולא שתות עצמה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:4:2.english: They rejoiced over one-sixth itself, etc. - For [regarding] that which we said, "From one-sixth to one-third according to Rabbi Tarfon is like one-sixth according to the Rabbis," they said [this referring to] from [more than] one-sixth and upward, and not [including] one-sixth itself.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:5:1.hebrew: אם תמצא לומר כו' - כלומר, אם באת לומר פשיטא דלעולם חוזר, דאי בכדי שיראה, מאי איכא כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:5:1.english: If you say, etc. - That is to say, if you come to say [that] it is obvious that he can always renege, for if [it were only] within the time that he can show [it], what [difference] is there, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:5:2.hebrew: איכא דאילו שתות כו' - כי נמי אמרינן תרוייהו בכדי שיראה, עדיין יש חילוק זה ביניהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:5:2.english: There is [a difference], as [for] one-sixth, etc. - Even when we say [that] both [are] within [the time] that he shows [it], there is still this distinction between them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:6:1.hebrew: משום הכי חזרו - מעיקרא, כי שוי להו ר' טרפון יתר על שתות אונאה — דלרבנן בטול מקח — ולא הרחיב זמן החזרה, שמחו בשתות עצמה, דמחילה לאלתר, כדאמרן. וכי הדר אמר להו כל היום, חזרו, דהחמיר להם ביתר על שתות, ופגם להם יותר ממה שהשביחם בשתות עצמה, כדפרישית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:6:1.english: Due to that they reverted - Initially, when Rabbi Tarfon deemed for them [an overcharge of] more than a sixth [to be] exploitation — which according to the Rabbis is nullification of the transaction — and had not [yet] extended the time for retraction, they rejoiced over a sixth itself, for [its] waiver is immediate, as we said. But when he subsequently told them [one may retract] the entire day, they reverted, because he was stringent on them regarding more than a sixth, and caused them greater loss than what he benefited them regarding a sixth itself, as I explained.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:6:2.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת לעולם חוזר - נהי נמי דשתות עצמה משוי להו אונאה כרבנן — דהאי דאמר לעיל שמחו בשתות עצמה שינויא דחיקא הוה, משום שמחה דמעיקרא דקשיא לן במאי שמחו, והשתא אמרת לי דשמחה מעיקרא משום בטול מקח היא דהואי, דלרבנן לעולם ולר' טרפון היו סבורין בכדי שיראה כדין אונאה דרבנן — כי הדר אמר להו כל היום, אכתי שמחה איכא, דלרבנן לעולם ולר' טרפון כל היום ותו לא. ואי משום שתות עצמה, דלרבנן בכדי שיראה ולדידיה כל היום — הרבה הוא שבח שמשביח רבי טרפון ביתר על השתות מפגם שפוגם בשתות עצמה, שהרי יכולין ליזהר בשתות עצמה: יפחתו לו מעט ותהא מחילה; נמצאו משתכרין בשל רבי טרפון כל אונאה שיתר על שתות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:6:2.english: But if you say [one can] always renege - Even though he [Rabbi Tarfon] treats a sixth itself as exploitation like the Rabbis — for that which [the Gemara] said above, "they rejoiced regarding a sixth itself," was a forced answer [given] because of the initial rejoicing, since we had a difficulty as to what they rejoiced over, whereas now you are saying to me that the initial rejoicing was because of nullification of the transaction, that according to the Rabbis [one can retract] forever, while according to Rabbi Tarfon they thought [it was only] within the time it takes to show [the merchandise], like the law of exploitation according to the Rabbis — when he then said to them "the entire day," there is still rejoicing, for according to the Rabbis [one can retract] forever and according to Rabbi Tarfon [only] the entire day and no more. And if [you object] regarding a sixth itself, that according to the Rabbis [one can claim it only] within the time it takes to show [it] while according to him [it is] the entire day — the advantage that Rabbi Tarfon gives them regarding more than a sixth is much greater than the disadvantage that he causes them regarding a sixth itself, for they can be careful regarding a sixth itself: they can reduce [the price] for him slightly and it will be waived; [thus] they end up profiting under Rabbi Tarfon's [ruling] in every [case of] exploitation that is more than a sixth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:7:1.hebrew: בטול מקח לא שכיח - ואין שבח זה חשוב להם במידי דלא שכיח, וכי מיקרי והוי נמי, הרי נתן לו שהות כל היום לחזור, ורוב הנמלכים נמלכים בו ביום. הלכך, פגם דשתות עצמה עדיף להו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:7:1.english: Nullification of the transaction is uncommon - And this advantage is not significant to them for something that is uncommon. And even when it does happen to occur, behold, [Rabbi Tarfon] gave him the entire day to retract, and most people who change their minds do so on that very day. Therefore, the disadvantage of [the] one-sixth itself matters more to them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:1.english: The halakha is: less than one-sixth, the merchandise is acquired - Immediately.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:2.english: Greater than one-sixth, the transaction is nullified - And both of them may retract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:3.english: One-sixth, [he] has acquired [it] - And neither of them can retract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:4.hebrew: ומחזיר אונאה - ולית ליה לרבא ידו על העליונה דמתניתין? דס"ל כר' נתן דברייתא, דקיימא לן ר' נתן דיינא הוא ונחית לעומקא דדינא, בפרק הבית והעלייה (לעיל בבא מציעא דף קיז: ובב"ק נג.):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:4.english: And returns [the] exploitation - Does Rava not hold [the principle that] he has the upper hand [as stated] in the Mishnah? [No,] for he holds in accordance with Rabbi Natan of the baraita, as we hold [that] Rabbi Natan is a judge and delves into the depths of the law, in the chapter [entitled] HaBayit VeHaAliyah (above, Bava Metzia 117b, and in Bava Kamma 53a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:5.english: This and that - Exploitation and nullification of the transaction.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:6.hebrew: יד מוכר על העליונה - אם נתאנה מוכר, והוא הדין אם נתאנה לוקח, יד לוקח על העליונה. והכי מוקמינן לה לקמן (בבא מציעא דף נא): מאי דשייר במתניתין תני בברייתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:6.english: The seller has the upper hand - [This applies] if the seller was exploited, and the same law [applies] if the buyer was exploited — the buyer has the upper hand. And so we establish it later on (Bava Metzia 51a): What [the Tanna] omitted in the Mishnah, he taught in the baraita.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 50b:9:7.english: This and that - Overcharge and nullification of the transaction.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 50b:10:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא מוכר לעולם חוזר משום הכי חזרו - אע"פ שגם תגרי לוד היו לוקחים ולא היה להם לחזור, מ"מ חזרו, משום דתגרי לוד היו מוכרים תמיד במעט מעט והיו לוקחים בבת אחת:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 50b:10:1.english: Granted, if you say [that] a seller may always renege, for that reason they reverted - Even though the merchants of Lod were also buyers and [thus] should not have reverted, nevertheless they reverted, because the merchants of Lod would always sell little by little and would buy all at once.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 50b:5:1.hebrew: ואילו יתר על שתות שניהם חוזרי' - וא"ת: דבפרק הספינה (ב"ב דף פג: ושם פד. ד"ה אי לא) אמר רב חסדא: מכר לו שוה ה' בו' והוקר ועמד על ח', לוקח יכול לחזור בו ולא מוכר, דאמר ליה לוקח: "אי לאו דאוניתני לא מצית הדר בך כו'". וה"נ, אמאי מאנה יכול לחזור? נימא ליה נמי המתאנה: "אי לאו דאוניתני כו'"! וי"ל: דהכא כיון שהוא יותר משתות ה"ל רחוק מן המקח יותר מדאי, וכאילו לא מכר כלל, דה"ל כיין ונמצא חומץ, חומץ ונמצא יין, דשניהם חוזרין (שם דף פג:). וה"ר יצחק בר' מרדכי תירץ: דהתם כשאין הלוקח תובע אונאתו, לכך אין המוכר יכול לחזור בו; אבל הכא מיירי כשמתאנה תובע אונאתו, ולכך המאנה יכול לבטל המקח:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 50b:5:1.english: Whereas [when the disparity is] greater than one-sixth, both can renege - And if you ask: In the chapter [entitled] HaSefinah (Bava Batra 83b, and ibid. 84a, s.v. "I lav"), Rav Chisda said: If one sold [an item] worth five for six, and its price rose and stood at eight, the buyer can retract and not the seller, because the buyer can say to him: "If you had not overcharged me, you would not be able to retract, etc." And here too, why can the one who overcharged retract? Let the exploited party also say to him: "If you had not exploited me, etc." And one can answer: Here, since it is more than one-sixth, it is too far from the [true] sale [price], and it is as if he did not sell [it] at all, for it is like [a sale of] wine and it was found to be vinegar, [or] vinegar and it was found to be wine, where both can retract (ibid., 83b). And Rabbi Yitzchak bar Rabbi Mordechai answered: There [it refers to a case] where the buyer is not claiming his overcharge; therefore the seller cannot retract. But here it speaks of [a case] where the exploited party is claiming his overcharge, and therefore the exploiting party can nullify the sale.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 50b:8:1.hebrew: אמר רבא הלכתא שתות קנה ומחזיר אונאה - פ"ה: קנה בע"כ כר' נתן דבסמוך. לפי זה, פחות משתות לאלתר הויא מחילה, וזה יש בין שתות לפחות משתות. וכן משמע לקמן (בבא מציעא דף נא.) גבי ההוא גברא דנקט ורשכי לזבוני, אמר: אי יהיבנא ליה חמשא ופלגא הויא מחילה, משמע דלאלתר הוי מחילה. ודקאמר "זה וזה בכדי שיראה", איתר משתות ושתות קאי, ולא אפחות משתות. ורבא אית ליה שפיר דרב חסדא, דקאמר בפ' הספינה (ב"ב דף פג:): מכר לו שוה ה' בו', לוקח יכול לחזור בו ולא מוכר; כיון שהוקר בכדי שיראה, שזהו זמן שלוקח יכול לתבוע אונאתו, והוקר על בטול מקח, לכך לוקח יכול לחזור בו. ולכך קאמר "ועמדו על ח'", ולא קאמר "ועמדו על ז'", שאין זה בטול מקח. וק' לר"ת: וכי חולק רבא על סתם מתניתין (לקמן בבא מציעא נא.), דקתני "מי שהוטל עליו ידו על העליונה"? ועוד, דהלכה כרבי מחבירו! ועוד, דרבא גופיה מוקי מתני' כר' יהודה הנשיא ולא כר' נתן; א"כ משמע דסבר ליה כוותיה! ועוד, מה שייך למימר "תניא כוותיה" בדבר שיש מחלוקת תנאים כתוב באותה ברייתא? ומפ' ר"ת: דרבא דאמר "שתות קנה", היינו אם רצה, כר' יהודה; ולא חש לפרש בהדיא "רצה", משום דקאי אמתני'. ו"תניא כוותיה" מייתי משום דקתני בברייתא "זה וזה בכדי שיראה", כדרבא; אבל מרבי יהודה הנשיא לא מייתי דאמר "רצה אמר לו כו'", דאדרבה ה"ל לאתויי מתניתין. ולקמן (בבא מציעא דף נא.) פריך שפיר: אי ר' נתן, מתניתין קתני "רצה", ברייתא לא קתני "רצה" — משום דר' נתן לא קאי אמתניתין וה"ל לפרושי; אבל רבא דקאי אמתני' לא חש לפרש. ואע"ג דרבא נקיט לישנא דמילתא דרבי נתן, אין פי' "קנה" דהכא כ"קנה" דרבי נתן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 50b:8:1.english: Rava said: The halakha is [that if the overcharge is] one-sixth, [the buyer] has acquired [the item] and [the overcharger] returns the overcharge - The Kuntres [i.e., Rashi] explains: [The buyer] has acquired [it] against his will, in accordance with Rabbi Natan [cited] immediately below. According to this, [an overcharge of] less than one-sixth is immediately [considered] a waiver, and this is [the difference] between one-sixth and less than one-sixth. And so it is implied below (Bava Metzia 51a) regarding that certain man who was holding silk strips to sell; [the buyer] said: "If I give him five and a half [ma'a], it is a waiver," which implies that [less than one-sixth] is immediately a waiver. And that which [Rava] says, "Both this and that [may be claimed] within the time it takes to show [it]," refers to greater than one-sixth and [exactly] one-sixth, and not to less than one-sixth. And Rava agrees well with [the ruling of] Rav Chisda, who says in Chapter HaSefinah (Bava Batra 83b): If one sold him [something] worth five for six, the buyer can retract and not the seller; since it appreciated within the time it takes to show [it] — which is the time during which the buyer can claim his overcharge — and it appreciated to [the level of] nullification of the transaction, therefore the buyer can retract. And for this reason [Rav Chisda] says "and it stood at eight," and does not say "and it stood at seven," because that is not [a case of] nullification of the transaction. And it is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: Does Rava disagree with an anonymous Mishnah (below, Bava Metzia 51a), which teaches: "Whoever was wronged has the upper hand"?! And furthermore, the halakha follows Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] over his colleague! And furthermore, Rava himself establishes the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and not in accordance with Rabbi Natan; if so, it implies that he holds like him! And furthermore, what relevance is there to saying "It was taught [in a baraita] in accordance with him" regarding a matter in which a Tannaitic dispute is written in that very baraita? Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explains: When Rava says "one-sixth, he has acquired [it]," that means if he wishes [to keep it], in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda [HaNasi]; and he did not bother to state "if he wishes" explicitly because he is referring back to the Mishnah. And [the Gemara] cites "It was taught in accordance with him" because the baraita teaches "Both this and that within the time it takes to show [it]," like Rava; however, it does not cite [this] from Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who says "if he wishes, he says to him, etc.," because on the contrary, it would have had to cite the Mishnah. And below (Bava Metzia 51a) [the Gemara] asks well: "If [the Mishnah follows] Rabbi Natan, the Mishnah teaches 'if he wishes,' whereas the baraita does not teach 'if he wishes'" — because Rabbi Natan is not referring back to our Mishnah, so he should have stated [it explicitly]; whereas Rava, who is referring back to our Mishnah, did not bother to state [it explicitly]. And even though Rava adopts the phrasing of Rabbi Natan's statement, the meaning of "he has acquired" here is not like "he has acquired" of Rabbi Natan.
